name: Song of Solomon

objectives.text: Identify the Song of Solomon as a book of the Bible that is a song about the love between a husband and wife
Explain that God created marriage as a good gift for a husband and wife
Locate the Song of Solomon among the poetry and wisdom books of the Old Testament and name Solomon as the king in its title
Identify the main voices in the Song as the bride, the bridegroom, and the daughters of Jerusalem
Describe how the bride speaks of her husband as both her beloved and her friend
Describe how the Song uses pictures from nature such as gardens, vineyards, flowers, and animals to express love
Explain from Scripture the Reformed tradition's teaching that marriage is a covenant between one man and one woman
Explain the meaning of the repeated charge not to stir up or awaken love until it pleases
Describe the faithful mutual belonging expressed in the refrain my beloved is mine and I am his
Analyze the Song's figurative language, including similes, metaphors, and descriptive praise poems of the bride and groom
Trace the movement of the Song through its scenes of longing, searching, and reunion
Explain how the Song presents physical intimacy within marriage as a good part of God's creation
Interpret the climactic description of love as strong as death and unquenchable by many waters
Explain the identity and role of the Shulammite woman in the Song
Explain why the church received the Song as canonical Scripture even though it rarely or never names God directly
Compare literal, allegorical, and typological approaches to interpreting the Song in Jewish and Christian history
Analyze how the prophets use marriage imagery for God's covenant with Israel as background for reading the Song
Evaluate contemporary cultural views of sexuality in light of the Song's portrait of exclusive covenant love
Evaluate how the Song functions as wisdom literature that instructs God's people in love and marriage
Compose an essay that synthesizes the Song with New Testament teaching on the church as the bride of Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: song about love, marriage as gift, poem about bride and groom (now naming its voices), friendship in marriage (anchored to 5:16), one man and one woman covenant, loyalty (now the mutual belonging refrain), poetic language, marital intimacy, Shulammite, literal vs allegorical, cultural views of sexuality, and bride of Christ synthesis. Dropped the generic objective that God loves His people, since it is not specific to this book. Folded the grade 5 comparison to God's love for the church into the grade 12 synthesis. Folded the defence of intimacy within marriage into the grade 8 and grade 11 objectives. Added objectives for locating the book in the canon, its nature imagery, the do not awaken love refrain, its structure of longing and reunion, the love strong as death passage, its canonicity, prophetic marriage imagery as background, and its function as wisdom literature. Added verse-level anchors and Westminster Confession 1.2, 24.1, 24.2, and 25.1 where they state the doctrine.
